cve_candidates.description: ReDoS / resource exhaustion in Werkzeug < 2.3.8 and < 3.0.1 via crafted multipart POST data with a malformed boundary string; version 2.3.7 falls within the affected range.

Werkzeug interactive debugger misconfiguration: when Flask runs in DEBUG mode (strongly indicated by port 5000 dev-server exposure and presence of /debug endpoint returning 200), the Werkzeug PIN-protected debugger console may be accessible, enabling unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Python console on unhandled exception pages (/__debugger__, /console). No single CVE assigned but widely documented critical misconfiguration.

attack_surface_summary:
The engagement target is a Linux host (10.10.20.30) running a Flask/Werkzeug 2.3.7 development server on port 5000/tcp — discovered exclusively via OSINT: a staging environment variable leaked in git commit history (commit 8728be547b) of the public repository github.com/laconic-mercenary/meridian-client-x. The public domain meridian.openintel.to is a CDN-fronted (Cloudflare) marketing site and is NOT the target.

The attack surface is narrow in port count (single open port) but extremely high in severity:

1. YAML Deserialization / Injection (CRITICAL): The /api/parse-config endpoint (POST, Content-Type: text/yaml) accepts raw user-supplied YAML documents server-side. The engineering blog explicitly states the portal 'parses submitted YAML configuration server-side.' Depending on the YAML library and load function used (e.g., PyYAML yaml.load() without Loader=SafeLoader), this is a direct Remote Code Execution vector via YAML deserialization gadgets.

2. Werkzeug Debug Mode RCE (CRITICAL): The /debug path returns HTTP 200 — a strong indicator the Flask application is running with DEBUG=True. In debug mode, Werkzeug exposes an interactive Python console on exception pages, enabling unauthenticated RCE. The dev server on port 5000 further corroborates debug/staging deployment.

3. CVE-2023-46136 DoS (HIGH): Werkzeug 2.3.7 is below the patched version (2.3.8), making it vulnerable to multipart boundary ReDoS.

4. No Authentication Layer: The client library's API call shows no Authorization headers or API keys — the YAML submission endpoint appears unauthenticated.

5. Secret Leakage via Git History: The staging host, port, and full API contract were recovered from immutable git history despite developer remediation — a systemic secrets management failure. The dark-web surface tier is clean (no credential dumps), but deeper tier sources were not queried per operator direction.
